statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures are halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is moderate at 36 as a carried rates, energy and geopolitical condition rather than an equity-structure one.
recommendation: The last observed session is consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z on Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly twenty-two hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the rates and energy backdrop. No danger window is carried, because none can be evidenced in a closed market. The first genuine price-path test falls outside this forecast and is scored by a later assessment.
headline: Second consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, leaving Friday's cash NDX close of 29,308.86, +0.33%, as the last observed Nasdaq-100 reference.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. That close snapped a five-day Nasdaq-100 losing streak, though the index still ended the week lower alongside the S&P 500 and the Dow. VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the base of a 14.77-15.95 range. The backdrop behind Stress is unchanged rather than improving: the 2-year closed at 4.24%, the 10-year at 4.74% and the 30-year at 5.28% after a week in which a Treasury buyback expansion produced only a short-lived rally before long-end yields rebuilt, with the 30-year having touched a nineteen-year high earlier in the week. WTI closed at $86.64 and Brent at $93.87 with Strait of Hormuz transit still curtailed and the U.S.-Iran impasse running through sanctions and economic pressure rather than fresh strikes; no new escalation has been verified since the halt. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context shows mixed megacap breadth at five of eight higher and net-negative semiconductors, which is confirmation context only and is not treated as evidence of live Nasdaq-100 structure. No U.S. macro release, Treasury auction or Fed appearance falls inside this horizon; the next checkpoint is Monday's Chicago Fed National Activity Index, followed by Wednesday's PCE and GDP prints, NVIDIA results on Wednesday evening and the Jackson Hole keynote on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 17 hourly assessments are available and 7 clock-hours, all in the 21 August overnight window, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the early overnight, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash open where the mode was published as event/whipsaw, a decay back to 13 through the afternoon, a brief 16 at 19:00Z for the concentrated August expiry close, then 10 once that close cleared without one-way extension, 5 as the futures halt took effect and 4 in each of the two fully closed hours that followed. Stress fell steadily from 59 to 37 across the same span while Confidence rose from 83 to 88 as verified evidence accumulated, easing to 84 in the final two slots as live price discovery ended.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the horizon ends at 23:00Z on Saturday, roughly twenty-two hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress eases from 36 to a 34 trough through the deep weekend hours and then drifts back to 39 by the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens; the carry behind it is unchanged, with a 30-year at 5.28% after a nineteen-year high earlier in the week, crude held up by curtailed Hormuz transit, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse now running through economic pressure rather than strikes. Confidence decays from 85 to 74 across the horizon, reflecting distance from the last verified observation rather than any weakness in the evidence gathered. No danger window is published, no US release, auction or Fed appearance falls inside the horizon, and the first genuine price-path test lies beyond it at the Sunday reopen.
